subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle.park@finedge.com>, Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@finedge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements

Hi Danielle / Natalie,

Thanks for the time today — I appreciated the overview of FinEdge's LLM use cases. Quick recap of the pain points, success criteria, and next steps so we stay aligned:

Pain points (from our call):
- PII in user prompts and uploaded documents that must never be stored in raw form
- Need for field-level redaction and deterministic tokenization for repro/analytics
- Audit and compliance requirements: 90-day raw retention (for now), 365-day redacted logs, and access/audit trails for data governance
- Current stack: GCP + BigQuery, logs forwarded to Splunk, in-house proxy for model calls

Success criteria for pilot:
- Configurable PII redaction at ingestion (field-level) with verifiable redaction proofs
- Audit logs that capture per-request metadata +/- redacted content for 365 days
- SOC 2 evidence and architecture review completed before production
- Latency < 300ms p99 for inference and cost targets consistent with your forecasting

Next steps / deliverables:
1) I will share (attached) our concise datasheet and an example audit log schema we use in other FinTech pilots.
2) Vivek and Dev to join the follow-up technical call to review redaction/tokenization options — can we do Thu, Jun 11 at 10am PT?
3) Please share the MA/PO template (we can review commercial and legal touches in parallel)

Attachments:
- redwood-datasheet.pdf (product + security highlights)
- ma-request-template.xlsx (procurement template you mentioned)

If anything above is inaccurate or missing, call it out and I'll update. Otherwise I'll get the audit log sample over by EOD tomorrow.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements

Hi Danielle,

Great questions — quick answers below and attachments attached.

- Field-level redaction: yes. We support configurable redaction rules at the request level (JSON path, regex, or named field). Redaction proofs (hashes + salt per-tenant) can be generated to support reconciliation without exposing raw values.
- Deterministic tokenization: we support HMAC-style tokenization with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for deterministic, non-reversible tokens. This is an opt-in feature for pilots with stricter audit requirements.
- Audit log sample: attached is a small sample (redwood-audit-logging-sample.json) showing schema, example events, and the redaction metadata we include (redacted_fields, hash_proofs, retention_ttl).

Operational notes:
- Retention: retention policies are configurable per-tenant and per-log-type. We can configure raw inputs to 90 days and redacted logs to 365 days as you requested. All retention actions are recorded in the audit trail.
- Access & export: role-based access controls for logs, with export hooks to your Splunk instance via secure transfer (TLS + mTLS) or direct BigQuery sink — we'll coordinate the exact connector with your infra team on the tech call.
- Compliance pack: I'll attach a SOC 2 readiness checklist and can schedule a short session with our security lead (Logan) if your legal team wants deeper review.

Next steps:
- I'll drop the audit log sample and a short runbook for the Jun 11 call (10am PT). Please confirm the attendee list and whether your Splunk engineer (for ingestion) can make the call.
- I'll also open a HubSpot deal (DEAL-2026-042) and link our docs: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/logging

Attachments:
- redwood-audit-logging-sample.json
- redwood-soc2-checklist.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

Best,
Marissa
